Executive Summary

On March 13, 2026, Pest Pro, LLC conducted a comprehensive initial assessment of the Rehabilitation Center of Orlando in the presence of Regional Maintenance Director Thomas and Chief Engineer George. The assessment revealed a well-established rodent infestation with evidence of sustained activity throughout the dietary kitchen, associated ceiling voids, and mechanical spaces above the primary food service areas.

The infestation exhibits characteristics consistent with a long-term presence, including extensive nesting material accumulation in above-ceiling spaces, rodent runway activity along wall junctions and equipment runs, gnaw damage to HVAC ductwork, and multiple active and unsealed structural penetration points throughout the facility.

Week 1 Status: Ahead of Schedule. Service commenced immediately following the initial assessment on March 13, 2026, with daily service visits conducted through March 19, 2026. The results achieved during Week 1 have exceeded our initial projections. Significant rodent activity has been intercepted and the program is currently ahead of the target timeline for full eradication. We are confident that this positive progress will continue throughout the remaining weeks of the program.

Scope of Services

This agreement authorizes Pest Pro, LLC to provide a comprehensive Rodent Eradication Program at the above-referenced facility. The program is designed to systematically eliminate the active rodent population, monitor for any remaining activity, and provide ongoing recommendations to prevent recurrence. All services are specific to rodents (rats and mice) unless otherwise noted in writing.

Services provided under this agreement include the deployment and monitoring of mechanical snap traps, glue boards, and pheromone-baited stations throughout identified active areas and travel routes. Commercial grade rodenticide will be applied in accordance with all applicable regulations for healthcare facilities. Commercial grade deodorizer will be applied to affected areas as needed. The client's approximately 80 existing exterior bait stations will be incorporated into the overall treatment program.

A written progress report will be provided at the conclusion of each service week, documenting observations, actions taken, captures recorded, and the recommended service schedule for the following week.

Target Areas of Service

Interior Primary Areas: Dietary kitchen and all associated food preparation and storage areas, office areas, and common areas throughout the facility.

Interior Secondary Areas: Drop ceiling voids, mechanical and HVAC spaces, and structural void spaces identified as active rodent travel corridors and harborage areas during the initial assessment.

Exterior Areas: Full building perimeter, roof penetrations including lead stacks, and all points where air conditioning equipment is secured to the structure.

Projected Completion: Full control of the rodent infestation is anticipated by Week 6 or sooner, contingent upon the timely completion of all client responsibilities, including repair of all interior and exterior structural penetrations, trimming of all trees, overhanging limbs, shrubs, and bushes away from the building, and removal of all debris from surrounding areas.

Client and Maintenance Staff Responsibilities

The effectiveness of this program and the ability to meet the projected timeline are directly dependent upon the cooperation and prompt action of the client's property management and maintenance staff. The following responsibilities must be fulfilled throughout the duration of this program.

  • Complete all exclusion work and structural repairs to seal all identified interior and exterior rodent entry points.
  • Ensure all trees, overhanging limbs, shrubs, and bushes are trimmed and maintained away from the building structure.
  • Remove and maintain all excess leaves and debris from all areas surrounding the building.
  • Maintain proper sanitation in all areas, including ceiling tile spaces and mechanical void areas.
  • All trash receptacles within the dietary kitchen must be emptied and discarded nightly. No food, even if covered, shall be left out in the dietary kitchen or any food preparation and storage areas after hours.
  • Report any observed pest activity to the designated site log or directly to the Pest Pro account manager without delay.
  • Ensure all doors and other points of entry are maintained and kept closed at all times to deter additional rodent entry.
  • Keep all dumpster areas, trash areas, and surrounding building entrances clear of discarded food and unsanitary debris.

Pest Pro Response Commitments

  • Any reported pest activity will be addressed within 24 hours of notice.
  • All calls and text messages will be returned within 4 hours.
  • A written weekly progress report will be provided at the conclusion of each service week, addressing observations, actions taken, and progress to date.

Week 1 Photo Documentation

The photographs included in this section were taken during the initial assessment on March 13, 2026, and throughout the Week 1 service period. They document the conditions observed, penetration points identified, evidence of rodent activity, and treatment results achieved. These images are provided as a visual record of the scope of the infestation and the progress made during the first week of the program.

Section A: Exterior Conditions and Harborage Areas

The following photographs document exterior conditions observed during the initial assessment on March 13, 2026. These conditions represent primary contributing factors to the sustained rodent infestation and must be addressed by maintenance staff as outlined in the client responsibilities section of this agreement.

Exterior building perimeter showing accumulated debris, overgrown vegetation, and moisture along the building foundation — a primary harborage corridor for rodents.

Section B: Interior Penetration Points and Entry Pathways

The photographs below document unsealed penetration points identified throughout the dietary kitchen and associated areas. Each of these locations represents an active or potential rodent entry and travel route within the facility. Remediation of these points by maintenance staff is critical to achieving lasting control.

Interior kitchen floor level showing an open structural penetration at the base of a column where the floor meets the wall. This unsealed gap serves as a direct rodent entry point into the building interior.
Interior ceiling-wall junction showing a displaced drop ceiling tile and unsealed gap at the concrete block wall, providing a direct access route between the ceiling void and the occupied space below.
Interior hallway wall-baseboard junction showing an unsealed structural penetration adjacent to an existing doorstop. This open gap leads from the hallway directly into the structural wall cavity and serves as an active rodent entry and travel point within the facility.

Section C: Evidence of Rodent Activity

The following photographs illustrate physical evidence of active and sustained rodent activity discovered throughout the facility during the initial assessment and subsequent service visits. The extent of contamination observed is consistent with a long-established infestation that has gone unaddressed for an extended period.

Visible rodent rub marks along the kitchen wall surface behind commercial equipment, indicating a heavily traveled runway with sustained rodent activity over an extended period.
Above-ceiling mechanical void above the dietary kitchen area. Extensive accumulation of rodent droppings, nesting debris, and organic matter indicating a long-established and heavily active nesting site.
HVAC flexible ductwork in the ceiling void showing rodent gnaw damage. Nesting material is visible inside the duct breach, indicating rodents have penetrated the HVAC system — presenting both a pest control and air quality concern.

Section D: Service Documentation and Treatment Results

The photographs below document Pest Pro's treatment methodology and the results achieved during Week 1 of the Rodent Eradication Program. The captures documented represent significant progress and confirm that our trap placement strategy and treatment approach are producing results ahead of the projected timeline.

Pest Pro technician conducting above-ceiling inspection in the dietary kitchen area, documenting penetration points and active rodent travel corridors in the ceiling void.
Mechanical snap trap deployed in the ceiling void above the dietary kitchen at an identified active travel route. Heavy rodent droppings visible in surrounding area confirm high activity at this location.
Norway rat captured on a snap trap placed on HVAC ductwork in the ceiling void above the kitchen. Surrounding contamination and nesting debris are visible, confirming an active above-ceiling rodent population.
Two rats captured on snap traps deployed within the kitchen equipment void. Surrounding nesting material and food debris confirm this area as an active harborage and breeding site within the facility.
Norway rat captured on a glue board deployed in the dietary kitchen area, documenting active rodent presence within the primary food service environment.

Pests Covered

This service agreement is specific to rodent eradication (rats and mice) at the above-referenced facility. This agreement does not cover roaches, bed bugs, fleas, poisonous or stinging insects, spiders, ants, snakes, or wildlife including raccoons, possums, or squirrels, unless otherwise specified in writing.

General Terms and Conditions

Limitation of Liability. Pest Pro, LLC liability for any damages is strictly limited to such damages as are directly caused by the negligence of the company or its authorized employees.

Resident and Employee Notification. It is understood and agreed that the primary responsibility rests with the property owners and managers to provide necessary information to all residents and employees regarding services being performed. Property owners and managers must inform all relevant parties if scented or chemical products will be in use during treatment. Upon receiving such notification, it is the responsibility of each individual to take any necessary personal precautions to ensure their own safety and well-being.

Service Results. Results of services rendered are strictly relative to and dependent upon the cooperation of the client as to sanitary conditions, maintenance, accessibility of the premises, and prompt reporting of pest activity. If the client does not cooperate as outlined in this agreement, service may continue but results cannot be assured and the client will be charged for any additional service required as a result.

Pesticide Usage. All pesticides anticipated for use are EPA-approved and will be applied in strict accordance with label directions and restrictions. Unless otherwise noted, all pest control applications at this facility will adhere to the recommended guidelines and protocols established for healthcare environments, including Adult Living Facilities (ALF), Adult Congregate Living Facilities (ACLF), skilled nursing homes, rehabilitation centers, and licensed healthcare facilities, as required by applicable state and federal regulations.

Equipment Replacement. Replacement of any damaged or missing equipment originally installed by Pest Pro, LLC will be replaced and invoiced at current rates.

Payment Terms. All invoices are due and payable within 30 days of issuance. Invoices will be issued on a weekly basis upon completion of each week's services.

Indemnification. Pest Pro, LLC agrees to indemnify and hold harmless the client, their agents, partners, and employees against any and all liability, including legal costs and expenses, on account of death or injury to any person or damage to property arising out of or in any way relating to the performance of this agreement, due to the sole negligence of Pest Pro, LLC, or their partners, employees, or agents.
